subject: Renewal: dedicated capacity + scaling guardrails for upcoming year
messages:
From: Emma Ruiz <emma.ruiz@acmecloud.com>

Cc: Procurement <procurement@acmecloud.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal discussion — reserved GPUs + scaling controls

Hi Aditya,

We're lining up our budget for 2027 and want to firm up the Dedicated renewal with Redwood. We are supportive of a 12-month renewal, but two points are blockers on our procurement side:

1) Throughput guarantees — we need a clearer SLA for sustained 99th-pct p50 token latency at our baseline workload (50M tokens/day).
2) Scaling guardrails — procurement requires a conservative min/max commitment and a documented warm pool policy (we currently can't tolerate >3m scale-up lag for peak events).

I've attached our internal ops note (high level) and would appreciate a proposal that shows: additional reserved GPUs (if any), the warm pool sizing approach, and an explicit min/max replica table per region. If you can include a small paragraph on fallbacks (regional failover / fallback to smaller quantized variants) for peak mitigation, that would help speed approvals.

Can we have a short call this week? Emma Ruiz, ACME Cloud — Platform Ops.

Thanks,
Emma

Attachments: acme-ops-opsnote.pdf (referenced)
From: aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Ruiz <emma.ruiz@acmecloud.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — reserved GPUs + scaling controls

Emma — thanks for the clear ask and the timeline.

Short answer: we can structure the renewal to include a modest uplift in reserved GPUs + a firm min/max and a warm pool commitment. I want to outline two pragmatic options before we jump to legal/procurement:

Option A (predictable throughput): +10 reserved A100 equivalents (regional split), min replicas = baseline capacity to meet 50M tokens/day, max replicas = baseline * 4 for controlled burst. Warm pool: 10% of max (pre-warmed instances with KV cache primed) with scale-up target < 3 minutes for small bursts, < 2 minutes for auto-managed critical bursts.

Option B (cost-lean): +6 reserved GPUs + larger burst allowed onto shared surge capacity (best-effort), min replicas = baseline, max replicas = baseline * 6 but with softer throughput SLA; warm pool: 5% of max, 3–5 minute expected scale.

I'm looping in Marissa (RPO/Customer Success) and Vivek (runtime/ops) to validate timing guarantees and the warm pool engineering commitments. If ACME legal wants a line in the SLA about model fallback (smaller quantized variants), we can add a rollback/fallback clause with a documented latency delta.

Let's do a 30-min sync tomorrow 10:00 PT? I can bring a high-level quote and sample SLA wording.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood-dedicated-proposal-v3.pdf (proposal draft)
From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 08:46:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — dedicated renewal scaling guardrails

Aditya / Marissa — quick engineering read:

- Warm pool sizing: 10% of peak (Option A) is reasonable for predictable bursts if ACME can tolerate the cost delta; we'll pre-warm instances with KV caches for top-20 prompt prefixes from their telemetry. That reduces effective scale-up to ~90s for token-streaming starts and ~2m for fully loaded warm-pool > cold-starts.
- Scale-up lag: hard SLO < 3 minutes for critical paths is feasible if we reserve a small set of on-demand GPUs in the region (hot spare). We'll need contractual commitment from ACME for a small monthly reserved uplift to justify hot spares.
- Min/Max replicas table: I'll attach a quick spreadsheet with baseline->max mapping by region and model family. See attached: scale-guardrails-diff-2026.xlsx.
- Fallbacks: we can auto-fallback to a quantized 8-bit variant with ~1.8x inference throughput (higher latency) — we'll place this in the SLA as a controlled fallback; logging and regression alerts will trigger a manual rollback if quality drops.

Risks: network egress patterns during failover, and cache priming dependencies on prefix distributions. We should include a short runbook: 'when warm pool < 60% primed, fall back to pre-defined smaller models + cold-cache warmers.'

I can join the call and walk through the spreadsheet.

— Vivek
VP, Serving Runtime Engineering
From: aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Ruiz <emma.ruiz@acmecloud.com>, Procurement <procurement@acmecloud.com>

Date: Wed, 08 Dec 2026 14:35:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal: dedicated capacity + scaling guardrails for upcoming year

Emma / ACME team — thanks again for the call this morning. Per our discussion, summary and agreed next steps below.

Agreed commercial structure (high level):
- 12-month renewal (Jan 1 — Dec 31, 2027).
- Reserved uplift: +8 A100-equivalent GPUs (regional allocation: 60% us-west, 40% us-east) — captured in the attached redlined proposal (redwood-dedicated-proposal-v3.pdf).
- Min/Max replicas: baseline = unit to support 50M tokens/day (documented in spreadsheet); min = baseline, max = baseline * 4 (hard cap).

Engineering / SLA commitments:
- Warm pool: 10% of max as pre-warmed instances with KV cache priming for top prefixes (target median scale-up 90s, 95th percentile < 3m for critical events).
- Scale-up lag: Hot-spare policy to meet < 3-minute SLO for critical traffic; requires the reserved uplift above to be in contract.
- Fallbacks: automatic fallback to quantized model variant (8-bit) when warm pool health < 60%; full tracing and a rollback runbook included.

Docs & next steps:
- I've uploaded the updated proposal and the guardrails spreadsheet to the HubSpot deal and attached the SLA term amendment for legal review.
- Action owners: Aditya — finalize commercial redlines; Marissa — coordinate procurement/legal redline loop; Vivek/Karthik — finalize warm pool runbook and instrumentation deliverables.
- Target sign: 2026-12-20 (procurement preference); DocuSign ready when legal signs off.

Please reply with any redline comments on the proposal or if you want a deeper walkthrough of the warm pool priming approach.

Best regards,
Aditya Rao
